A.explanation: The ratio $k/m$ has units $\text{s}^{-2}$, so $T$ would have units $\text{s}^{-2}$ not $\text{s}$.

B.explanation: The ratio $m/k$ has units $\text{s}^{2}$, so $T$ would have units $\text{s}^{2}$ not $\text{s}$.

C.explanation: The ratio $k/m$ has units $\text{s}^{-2}$, so its square root has units $\text{s}^{-1}$ which is frequency not period.

D.explanation: The ratio $m/k$ has units $\text{s}^{2}$, so its square root has units $\text{s}$, matching period $T$.

hints: Notice the left side $T$ is a period, so it must have base unit $\text{s}$, while $m$ has unit $\text{kg}$.
Find the base units of spring constant $k$ from $F = kx$ in the mass-spring diagram, where force is in $\text{N}$ and extension $x$ is in $\text{m}$.
Form the combination $m/k$ and check whether you need the ratio itself or its square root to leave only $\text{s}$.
walkthrough: Left side: period $T$ has unit $\text{s}$, which in base units is $\text{s}$.
Right side quantities: mass $m$ has unit $\text{kg}$. From $k = F/x$, $k$ has units $\text{N m}^{-1} = (\text{kg m s}^{-2})\text{m}^{-1} = \text{kg s}^{-2}$.
To obtain $\text{s}$ to match $T$, take the square root: $\sqrt{m/k}$ has units $\text{s}$. The constant $2\pi$ has no units.
The inverted ratio $k/m$ gives $\text{s}^{-2}$ and its square root gives $\text{s}^{-1}$, so those forms cannot match $T$.
Only $T = 2\pi\sqrt{m/k}$ is homogeneous. This is option D.
